intro: The Ravens lost Lamar Jackson and went shopping for a quarterback, the Browns turn to Shedeur Sanders, and Myles Garrett is set to debut for the Rams. Sunday brings Packers at Patriots and a slate full of injury questions. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Ravens trade for Jacoby Brissett after Lamar Jackson goes down
top.dek: Baltimore sent Arizona a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh, and got a 2027 fifth back. The deal follows a four-game losing streak and injuries to both Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The Ravens have not said whether Brissett starts.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Deshaun Watson stays in the concussion protocol, Sanders starts
top.dek: Watson reported symptoms Monday night after a helmet hit from Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker. He practiced on a limited basis Friday but has not been cleared and is not expected to play. Shedeur Sanders takes the Week 9 start for Cleveland.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Myles Garrett expected to make his Rams debut at Washington
top.dek: Garrett played Week 1 in Australia, then had knee surgery and went on injured reserve. His practice window opened this week, and Sean McVay expects him to play Sunday barring setbacks.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 0: pass completions in a Buccaneers win, a first since 1974
top.dek: Tampa Bay beat Atlanta 16-0 without a completion, the first team to win that way since Buffalo on Sept. 29, 1974. The Bucs ran for 324 yards, a single-game team record, and kicker Chase McLaughlin is 19 for 19 on field goals.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Packers visit Patriots on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET
top.dek: Green Bay plays at Gillette Stadium on Fox against New England (5-3). Drake Maye has accounted for at least three touchdowns in five straight games, and A.J. Brown is out for the Patriots.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Allen passes Kelly as Bills roll to 6-1

stories.text: Josh Allen passes Jim Kelly for Bills TD record
stories.summary: Allen threw two touchdown passes in a 36-10 win over Baltimore on Nov. 1. The second was his 259th as a Bill, the most in franchise history. Buffalo improved to 6-1 and held the Ravens to 10 points.

stories.text: Bills line and receiver room thin before Monday night
stories.summary: Left tackle Dawkins missed Thursday and Friday practice with a rib injury, and right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. Receiver Joshua Palmer sat out with a hamstring, and Khalil Shakir is out for personal reasons. Tight end Dalton Kincaid moved up to full participation.

stories.text: Dalton Kincaid goes for 86 yards and a score
stories.summary: Kincaid caught four of six targets for 86 yards and a touchdown against Baltimore. He was limited with a chest injury Thursday and practiced fully Friday, a good sign for Monday.

stories.text: 12: QB hits by the Bills defense against Baltimore
stories.summary: Buffalo hit the Ravens quarterbacks 12 times and recorded four sacks. Rookies Landon Jackson and TJ Parker each got their first career sack. Kicker Tyler Bass also stretched his streak to 19 straight field goals.

stories.text: Bills visit Vikings on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at Minnesota on Monday, Nov. 9, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Watch the offensive line, with Dawkins and Brown both in question against a Vikings pass rush.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins try to find a run game without Achane

stories.text: Dolphins run game must replace De'Von Achane
stories.summary: Achane is on injured reserve and out for the season, so Ollie Gordon II becomes the lead back. The Dolphins fell to 1-6 after a 24-19 loss to New England on Nov. 1, when the ground game stalled.

stories.text: Backup backs and Willis practice with ailments
stories.summary: Running back Jaylen Wright was upgraded to limited Thursday after missing Wednesday with a quad injury. Kaytron Allen, Zach Sieler and Chop Robinson were also limited. Quarterback Malik Willis and rookie guard Kadyn Proctor, who cleared concussion protocol, practiced fully.

stories.text: Malik Willis throws for 211 yards behind a leaky line
stories.summary: Willis completed 21 of 32 passes for 211 yards and two touchdowns against New England, including a 35-yard strike to Kevin Coleman Jr. late. He was sacked five times and threw one interception.

stories.text: 74: Dolphins rushing yards against New England
stories.summary: Miami ran for 74 yards in Week 8, ending a run of games with at least 100. The team had 217 against Cincinnati in Week 5 and 156 against the Jets in Week 7.

stories.text: Dolphins host Lions on Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Miami hosts Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. The Lions rank 32nd against the pass but ninth against the run, so watch whether Willis can attack through the air.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots rally past Miami, host Packers next

stories.text: Patriots rally from 10 down to beat Miami 24-19
stories.summary: New England trailed 13-3 at halftime and scored all three of its touchdowns after the break. The win moved the Patriots to 5-3 and gave them four wins in their last five games.

stories.text: Henry questionable, Brown and Henderson out
stories.summary: Tight end Hunter Henry (foot) is questionable after leaving the Miami game. Receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson are listed out. Receiver Mack Hollins (calf) is eligible to return from injured reserve.

stories.text: Drake Maye accounts for three touchdowns again
stories.summary: Maye went 16 of 20 for 199 yards with two touchdown passes and a rushing score against Miami. All three came in the second half. He has 17 touchdowns and two interceptions over his last five games.

stories.text: 15: Patriots giveaways, third-most in the NFL
stories.summary: New England has turned it over 15 times this season. Maye had seven turnovers in his first three games and only three in the five since. Green Bay's defense has 15 takeaways, second in the league.

stories.text: Packers visit Gillette on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. on Fox
stories.summary: New England hosts Green Bay (5-3) on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. It is the first meeting since 2022. Watch Christian Gonzalez against Packers deep threat Christian Watson.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets hit Kansas City on a three-game skid

stories.text: Jets fall to Raiders 38-33 for third straight loss
stories.summary: The Jets dropped to 2-6 after giving up a 95-yard kickoff return touchdown and failing to force a turnover. Geno Smith threw an interception on the game's final play. Las Vegas went 4 for 4 in the red zone.

stories.text: Wilson and Wallace out; Hall and Bailey no designation
stories.summary: Receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) are out against the Chiefs. Breece Hall (quad) and David Bailey (groin) practiced fully Friday with no designation. Edge Joseph Ossai, safety VJ Payne, lineman Harrison Phillips and corner Nahshon Wright are questionable.

stories.text: Braelon Allen runs for 147 yards in Hall's absence
stories.summary: Allen carried 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown against Las Vegas while Hall sat out a fourth straight game. He could share carries with Hall now that Hall is practicing in full.

stories.text: 23: sacks taken by Geno Smith through eight games
stories.summary: Smith has been sacked 23 times this season but has still played well, according to the Jets' beat coverage. Kansas City's pass rush posted a season-low 6 percent pressure rate in Week 8, which gives the line a chance to hold up.

stories.text: Jets visit Chiefs on Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: New York plays at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. The Chiefs are 5-2 and coming off losses to Seattle and Denver. Kansas City running back Walker has 770 yards, and the Jets allow 5.03 yards per play.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens get Brissett as losses hit four

stories.text: Ravens trade for Jacoby Brissett after Lamar Jackson goes down
stories.summary: Baltimore finished a deal with Arizona on Friday for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, sending a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick and getting a 2027 fifth back. The move follows a four-game losing streak and the loss of both Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The team has not said whether Brissett will start.

stories.text: Jackson on IR after thumb surgery, Huntley done for the year
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson hurt his right thumb after one offensive play in his return against Buffalo on Nov. 1 and had surgery. He is on injured reserve with no return date. Backup Tyler Huntley has a toe injury that is reported to end his season.

stories.text: Justice Hill supplies the lone bright spot with a 65-yard score
stories.summary: Hill broke a 65-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter of Thursday's 33-10 loss to Jacksonville. It was Baltimore's only trip to the end zone in a game where undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his first NFL start and threw two interceptions. Hill gave the offense its only real chunk play.

stories.text: 4: straight losses for a Ravens team now 4-5
stories.summary: Baltimore has dropped four in a row, the latest a 33-10 home loss to the Jaguars in the rain. The Ravens managed just over 200 net yards and Jacksonville forced three turnovers. The previous week, a 36-10 loss to Buffalo, produced fewer than 100 combined passing yards.

stories.text: Chargers visit Baltimore on Nov. 16
stories.summary: The Ravens host the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16, the first game after the Brissett trade. Watch who takes the snaps and whether the offense can move the ball with a new quarterback learning the system on a short week. The source did not list kickoff time or network.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals open Madrid trip with edge rusher hurt

stories.text: Bengals head to Madrid with a first-place chase on the line
stories.summary: Cincinnati arrives at the Bernabeu at 5-2 after a 43-36 overtime win over Tennessee. The Bengals are trying to reach 6-2 before they host first-place Pittsburgh. The offense, led by Joe Burrow, drives the whole plan.

stories.text: Howell, Johnson and Turner all questionable for Atlanta
stories.summary: Rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell had wrist surgery, and no timetable has been given. Edge Cedric Johnson and cornerback DJ Turner II are also questionable. Wide receiver Andrei Iosivas remains on injured reserve.

stories.text: Tee Higgins sits second in the league with 726 receiving yards
stories.summary: Higgins has piled up 726 yards through seven games, second in the NFL. He caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the overtime win over the Titans. He pairs with Ja'Marr Chase, who added 11 catches for 141 yards in that game.

stories.text: 462: Joe Burrow's passing yards against Tennessee
stories.summary: Burrow completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards and five touchdowns, with three interceptions, in the 43-36 overtime win. He leads the league in completion percentage at 73%. Sources differ on his touchdown total (26 per BVM Sports, 20 per SI), so check before citing it.

stories.text: Falcons in Madrid, Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
stories.summary: Cincinnati faces Atlanta (3-5) at the Santiago Bernabeu in Madrid. The Falcons are coming off a 16-0 loss to Tampa Bay. After the trip the Bengals host Pittsburgh on Nov. 15.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Sanders starts as Watson sits with concussion

stories.text: Shedeur Sanders will start against the Saints
stories.summary: Coach Todd Monken said Sanders takes over in Week 9 while Deshaun Watson remains in the concussion protocol. Dillon Gabriel would likely back him up. Sanders has thrown three passes this season.

stories.text: Watson in concussion protocol after helmet hit
stories.summary: Watson reported symptoms Monday night after a helmet-to-helmet hit from Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker in the Week 8 loss. The Browns placed him in the protocol Tuesday. He practiced on a limited basis Friday but has not been cleared and is not expected to play.

stories.text: Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards
stories.summary: The tight end led Cleveland in the 27-6 loss at Pittsburgh with 10 catches and 154 yards. He also lost a fumble. The Browns will need him as a safety valve for a new starting quarterback.

stories.text: 33: sacks Watson has taken, most among all quarterbacks
stories.summary: Watson leads every quarterback in sacks taken after eight games. Pittsburgh sacked him eight times Sunday, a season high for Cleveland, and the Browns ran for only 34 yards. Whoever starts faces the same protection issues.

stories.text: Saints, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cleveland (5-3) hosts New Orleans in Week 9. Watch whether Sanders can protect the ball and whether the ground game improves after gaining 34 yards against Pittsburgh.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers hold AFC North lead heading into bye

stories.text: Steelers take sole control of the AFC North
stories.summary: Pittsburgh beat Cleveland 27-6 for its fourth straight win and moved to 6-2. It was the 23rd straight regular-season home win over the Browns. The Steelers now rest on their bye week in first place.

stories.text: Joseph-Day on IR with triceps injury, return unlikely
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day went on injured reserve Oct. 22 with a triceps injury. Outside linebacker Jack Sawyer's comments suggest he may not come back this season. Head coach Mike McCarthy has said IR players could still return in 2026.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren runs for 143 yards on 17 carries
stories.summary: Warren matched his career high against Cleveland. He has 704 rushing yards on the season at 5.9 yards a carry and also ranks as Pittsburgh's second-leading receiver with 25 catches. Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 8: sacks the Steelers piled up on Deshaun Watson
stories.summary: Pittsburgh sacked Watson eight times and took the ball away twice. Patrick Queen had 12 tackles and 1.5 sacks, and T.J. Watt added two sacks to push his career total against Cleveland to 20.5. The Browns ran for just 34 yards.

stories.text: Bye in Week 9, then at Bengals on Nov. 15
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is off this week. The Steelers visit Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Nov. 10 trade deadline could bring receiver help, since D.K. Metcalf has 33 catches for 378 yards.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans need a fix after the bye

stories.text: Texans return from bye at 2-5 with a winless Chargers team next
stories.summary: Houston sits 2-5 after its Week 8 bye and heads to SoFi Stadium to face the Chargers, the league's only winless team at 0-7. The Texans use the trip to show they fixed the tackling, penalty and communication problems that left them among the worst in the league at allowing explosive plays.

stories.text: Noel done for the year, Dell back in the receiver mix
stories.summary: Receiver Jaylin Noel went on injured reserve with a toe injury and will miss the rest of the season. Tank Dell returned just before the bye and should pick up some of that workload. The last official pre-bye report listed Reed Blankenship, Blake Fisher, David Montgomery and Jalen Pitre as out, so check Friday's report for Week 9 designations.

stories.text: C.J. Stroud protects the ball while taking hits
stories.summary: Stroud has completed 160 of 247 passes for 1,867 yards, 11 touchdowns and one interception, good for a 100.7 rating. He has also absorbed 15 sacks, so keeping him upright on early downs is the first job against Los Angeles.

stories.text: 27: Straight Chargers drives without a touchdown
stories.summary: The Chargers have gone 27 consecutive offensive possessions without a touchdown, and quarterback Justin Herbert has thrown 10 interceptions in seven games. Houston owns a +3 turnover margin, while Los Angeles sits at -6, which gives the Texans a chance to win the field position battle.

stories.text: At Chargers, Sunday 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Houston plays at the 0-7 Chargers at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8. Watch how the Texans use Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Nico Collins together, and whether the offense leans less on its six-lineman packages.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts open for business on Jonathan Taylor

stories.text: Giants emerge as lead suitor for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor
stories.summary: The Giants are reportedly the most serious bidder for Taylor, though they have not met Indianapolis's price of about a first-round pick. The Colts reportedly turned down a second-rounder plus another asset, then signaled they could lower the ask to a second. A deal is unlikely before Week 9 ends, with the Nov. 10 trade deadline close.

stories.text: Five Colts sit out Wednesday practice, Taylor limited
stories.summary: Keenan Allen and Charvarius Ward Sr. got rest days, while Akeem Davis-Gaither, Drew Ogletree and Justin Walley sat with knee injuries. Taylor was limited for rest. Bryce Boettcher (groin) and Anthony Gould (concussion), both out in Week 8, practiced fully.

stories.text: Daniel Jones keeps the job after a 42-7 loss
stories.summary: Coach Shane Steichen said Jones starts against Dallas, even after a Week 8 loss to Jacksonville in which he went 19 of 28 for 144 yards with two interceptions and four sacks. Jones has nine interceptions this season. Steichen said the offensive problems go beyond the quarterback, and Anthony Richardson only entered late with the game decided.

stories.text: 31st: Where the Colts offense ranks in expected points added
stories.summary: Indianapolis ranks 31st in offensive expected points added, per the TSN report on the Jacksonville loss. Jones posted a 39.6 QBR in that game, the second-worst mark of his eight seasons. Steichen pointed to route discipline, blocking and protections as shared problems.

stories.text: Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium, Sunday 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Indianapolis hosts Dallas on Sunday, Nov. 8, after trading away DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson. Dallas ranks seventh in offensive EPA per play while the Colts rank 28th by one measure, and the Cowboys are missing several defensive backs with injuries. Watch whether Taylor plays at all.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars rout Ravens, lead South by 3.5

stories.text: Jaguars beat Ravens 33-10 to build a 3.5-game division lead
stories.summary: Jacksonville never trailed in Baltimore on Thursday night and improved to 6-2, its fourth win in five games. The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 319 to 227 and forced three turnovers against a Baltimore team starting rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback. The Texans, at 2-5, trail by 3.5 games.

stories.text: Murray and Hamilton out for the season, line help sought
stories.summary: Coach Liam Coen confirmed that safety Eric Murray and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton are finished for 2026, and both went on injured reserve. Hamilton tore his quad in Week 8. Edge Travon Walker (rib) and running back Bhayshul Tuten (foot and ankle) were questionable Thursday and played through it.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence is sharp, Parker Washington hits a 50-yard TD
stories.summary: Lawrence went 16 of 26 for 242 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions, lifting his season line to 18 touchdown passes and four picks. Washington caught a 50-yard score that made it 17-3 at halftime. Coen called Lawrence extremely sharp and accurate when the game mattered.

stories.text: 31: Points or more in each of the Jaguars' last three games
stories.summary: Jacksonville has scored at least 31 points in three straight games, and all three were played in wet weather. Coen said the rain tests a team's physical and mental toughness. The Jaguars also held Derrick Henry to 57 yards on 17 carries, with 51 of those yards coming in the first half.

stories.text: At Titans, Sunday Nov. 15, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Jacksonville travels to Nissan Stadium to face a Tennessee team that is 1-7 and coming off its bye. The Jaguars have no game this weekend and use the extra days to heal. Watch the defensive line, which lost Hamilton, and whether the team adds help before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans hit the bye 1-7 after Simmons trade

stories.text: Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to Bears for two first-round picks
stories.summary: Tennessee sent the All-Pro defensive tackle to Chicago for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks plus a 2027 fourth-rounder, and got a 2028 fifth back going the other way. Simmons entered Week 8 with 28 pressures, the most among defensive tackles. The trade leaves the Titans rebuilding at 1-7.

stories.text: Four Titans hurt in Cincinnati, update due Nov. 11
stories.summary: Right tackle JC Latham (finger), left guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), cornerback Marcus Harris (ankle) and linebacker James Williams Sr. (groin) were hurt against the Bengals, and Skoronski and Harris left on carts. Receiver Carnell Tate missed that game with a shoulder injury and is expected back for Week 10. The next injury update is due Nov. 11.

stories.text: Cam Ward posts his first 300-yard game in OT loss
stories.summary: Ward threw for 304 yards and two touchdowns with a 104.6 rating in a 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati, his first 300-yard day. Coach Robert Saleh called it a step. Without Tate, Ward spread the ball to seven receivers, and Tony Pollard ran for 117 yards.

stories.text: 5: Amani Hooker's NFL-leading interception total
stories.summary: Hooker leads the league with five interceptions after picking off three passes in Cincinnati. The Titans forced four turnovers in that game, yet still gave up 510 yards and a season-high 43 points. Six of their eight games have been decided by one score.

stories.text: Bye in Week 9, then Jaguars at home Nov. 15
stories.summary: Tennessee is off this weekend. It returns Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX to host AFC South leader Jacksonville at Nissan Stadium. The NFL trade deadline falls on Nov. 10, so more roster moves could come before then.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos own the AFC West after comeback

stories.text: Broncos rally past Chiefs to take sole possession of first place
stories.summary: Denver erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat Kansas City 28-24 and improve to 6-2. Bo Nix threw two touchdowns, including a fourth-down score to Nate Adkins. The win dropped the Chiefs out of first place in the AFC West.

stories.text: Three Broncos out at Carolina, Hufanga questionable
stories.summary: Cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, safety Brandon Jones and lineman Eyioma Uwazurike are out after three straight days without practice. Safety Talanoa Hufanga is questionable after limited work, his first practices since a Week 5 ankle injury. Receiver Pat Bryant practiced fully and can be activated from injured reserve.

stories.text: Bo Nix keeps winning the fourth quarter
stories.summary: Nix went 20 of 32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns against Kansas City. Since he entered the league in 2024 he leads the NFL with 15 game-winning drives and 12 fourth-quarter comebacks. He has not thrown an interception in five straight games.

stories.text: 164: Nix's pass attempts without an interception
stories.summary: Nix's current streak of 164 straight attempts without a pick ranks sixth in Broncos history. His five straight games without an interception tie for the second-longest run in team history.

stories.text: At Carolina Sunday, then the bye
stories.summary: Denver visits the Panthers on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the receiver room, where Bryant could return to join Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton. The Broncos then take their Week 10 bye before hosting the Raiders.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs look to stop a two-game slide

stories.text: Chiefs blow a fourth-quarter lead and drop a second straight
stories.summary: Kansas City lost 28-24 to Denver after leading by 11 late in the third quarter. Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal in the fourth. On the last play the Chiefs could not score from the 1-yard line, and Patrick Mahomes was sacked as time expired.

stories.text: Mahomes, Kelce and Rice have no designation vs. Jets
stories.summary: Defensive tackles Peter Woods and Omarr Norman-Lott and cornerback Mansoor Delane are out. Receiver Nikko Remigio is questionable with a hip injury. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee), tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) and receiver Rashee Rice carry no designation.

stories.text: Emmett Johnson turns a short catch into 73 yards
stories.summary: Johnson's 73-yard touchdown catch gave Kansas City a 17-13 lead over Denver. It was the biggest play of a game the Chiefs eventually lost, and it marks Johnson as a real receiving threat out of the backfield.

stories.text: 24-13: the Chiefs' lead entering the fourth quarter
stories.summary: Kansas City had Denver down by 11 going into the final period and still lost. The Chiefs opened 5-0 and have now dropped two straight.

stories.text: Jets visit Arrowhead on Sunday
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Jets receiver Garrett Wilson is out with a concussion, which should help a Chiefs defense missing two tackles and a starting corner.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders snap skid, head to San Francisco

stories.text: Raiders end four-game losing streak with 38-33 win over Jets
stories.summary: Las Vegas trailed 23-14 at halftime and scored the last 15 points, including a field goal with 27 seconds left. Jeremy Chinn intercepted Geno Smith to seal it. The win moved the Raiders to 4-4.

stories.text: DT Thomas Booker out against the 49ers
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Thomas Booker did not practice all week and will miss the trip to San Francisco. He has played 38 percent of the Raiders' defensive snaps this season. No other Raiders player is listed as questionable.

stories.text: Kirk Cousins plays clean in the win
stories.summary: Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards with no turnovers against the Jets. Coach Klint Kubiak kept him as the starter over first-round pick Fernando Mendoza. Cousins also has 19 passing touchdowns, second in the league.

stories.text: 221: points the Raiders have scored through eight games
stories.summary: That total ranks second in the league and is the most for Las Vegas through eight games since 2002. Mike Washington Jr. ran for a career-high 83 yards on 25 carries last week while Ashton Jeanty had two carries.

stories.text: At the 49ers on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: The Raiders play at Levi's Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. San Francisco is missing three receivers, including Mike Evans. Watch whether Las Vegas keeps leaning on Washington on the ground.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers search for answers at 0-7

stories.text: Chargers fall to 0-7 after 24-9 loss to Rams
stories.summary: The Rams scored 21 straight points after a slow start to beat Los Angeles. Justin Herbert threw two interceptions, and the Chargers settled for three field goals on fourth-down attempts. It is their first 0-7 start since 2000.

stories.text: Slater and James on IR, Alt back at left tackle
stories.summary: Tackle Rashawn Slater and safety Derwin James Jr. are both on injured reserve. Joe Alt returned in Week 8 after missing two games and moved to left tackle, where he allowed no pressures against the Rams.

stories.text: Joe Alt anchors a patchwork line
stories.summary: Alt has allowed four pressures and no sacks over 169 pass-blocking snaps this season. Jim Harbaugh said Alt did a heck of a job sliding over to left tackle against the Rams.

stories.text: 27: straight Chargers drives without a touchdown
stories.summary: It is the longest such stretch since the 2024 Dolphins. Herbert has thrown 10 interceptions, tied for most in the league, and Los Angeles has just nine touchdowns all season, the fewest in the NFL.

stories.text: Texans visit SoFi on Sunday
stories.summary: Los Angeles hosts the 2-5 Houston Texans on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The Chargers' line must handle Will Anderson Jr., who shares the league lead with 7.5 sacks.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys blow lead, face Colts at 3-5

stories.text: Cowboys blow a two-score lead and fall to Arizona in overtime
stories.summary: Dallas led 27-17 with about five minutes left and lost 33-30. Arizona scored touchdowns on four straight possessions after Gardner Minshew replaced Jacoby Brissett late in the third quarter. Chad Ryland kicked a 42-yard field goal in overtime to finish it, and the Cowboys went three-and-out on their extra possession.

stories.text: Pickens and Porter Jr. questionable for Colts game
stories.summary: Wideout George Pickens (hamstring) and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) are questionable for Sunday, along with linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, tight end Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker. Rookie Malachi Lawrence (ankle) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) are out. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke cleared concussion protocol.

stories.text: Quinnen Williams piles up two more sacks against Arizona
stories.summary: Williams had two sacks in the loss, which gives him a team-high five this season. The Cowboys sacked Arizona five times and forced two turnovers, including a Shemar James interception. The defense held up until the Cardinals changed quarterbacks.

stories.text: 39.6: passer rating against Joey Porter Jr. in coverage
stories.summary: Porter has allowed 3 catches on 10 targets since Dallas acquired him after Week 4. He played 94 percent of Pittsburgh's snaps last year but only 53 percent in Dallas, as injuries have limited him. His ankle is the one to watch this week.

stories.text: At Colts, Sunday 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Dallas visits Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis at 3-5, and a loss would drop them to 3-6. Watch whether the secondary gets Porter and Downs back together. The Cowboys lead the all-time series 11-6.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lead the East heading to Philly

stories.text: Giants enter Week 9 as the NFC East's best team
stories.summary: At 4-2-1, New York climbed from 17th to 14th in Fox Sports' power rankings. The writer credits the running game and the coaching staff. The Giants now play a banged-up Eagles team in Philadelphia.

stories.text: Skattebo doubtful, Nabers practices ahead of Eagles
stories.summary: Running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) missed practice for a third straight day and is doubtful, though John Harbaugh left the door slightly open. Receiver Charlie Jones (hand) is questionable. Malik Nabers said he practiced Friday and no Giant is ruled out.

stories.text: Nabers named NFC Offensive Player of the Month
stories.summary: Nabers caught 36 passes for 509 yards and two touchdowns in four October games. He led the NFL in receiving yards through the month and ran off four straight 100-yard games. He is the only player this season with 500 yards and 35 catches in a four-game span.

stories.text: 2013: the last time the Giants won in Philadelphia
stories.summary: New York last won at the Eagles on October 27, 2013. The teams split their 2025 series, and the Eagles won the most recent meeting 38-20. J.J. McCarthy is chasing a third straight game with 240 passing yards and a 90 rating.

stories.text: At Eagles, Sunday 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Giants visit Lincoln Financial Field with a chance to stretch their division lead. Philadelphia starts third-string quarterback Joe Milton. Watch how New York's run game fares if Skattebo sits.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles turn to Joe Milton at QB

stories.text: Eagles bench Tanner McKee for Joe Milton III
stories.summary: Nick Sirianni told McKee he was out a day after saying he would stay the starter. Milton, who joined the team less than three weeks ago, makes his first career start Sunday against the Giants. Jalen Hurts remains out with blood clots.

stories.text: Six Eagles out, McKee questionable with ribs
stories.summary: DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) are all out against the Giants. McKee is questionable with a rib injury. Hurts has been on injured reserve since Oct. 17 and is expected to miss the season.

stories.text: Jalen Carter keeps wrecking games on a losing team
stories.summary: Carter had five tackles, a sack and a pass breakup in Week 8. Teammate Nolan Smith also recorded a sack, his third in four games. The defense has little else to show during a six-game skid.

stories.text: 0-3: Eagles record in Tanner McKee's starts
stories.summary: McKee completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 638 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions in losses to Carolina, Dallas and Washington. His passer rating was 76.6. DeVonta Smith, Wicks and Saquon Barkley all missed time in that stretch.

stories.text: Home vs. Giants, Sunday 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Philadelphia hosts the division-leading Giants at Lincoln Financial Field with a six-game losing streak. Milton makes his first start. Watch how the offense functions without Smith and Wicks.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders end skid, host Rams

stories.text: Commanders rally from 10-0 to beat Eagles 27-10
stories.summary: Washington scored 27 unanswered points on Sunday night. Jayden Daniels spoke to the offense after the early deficit, and the group scored on four of its next six drives. Dan Quinn liked that the frustration came from players other than his quarterback.

stories.text: Burks and Brown out, Newton questionable vs. Rams
stories.summary: Receivers Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) are out, and defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) is questionable. Daniels (left elbow), Sam Cosmi (knee) and Shy Tuttle (shoulder) carry no designation. Terry McLaurin is out for the season.

stories.text: Daniels steadies the offense with a thin receiver room
stories.summary: Daniels completed 55 percent of his passes for 217 yards against Philadelphia and threw a touchdown to Stefon Diggs. He returned in Week 5 from a dislocated elbow. Antonio Williams is emerging as his second option.

stories.text: 27: unanswered points that sank the Eagles
stories.summary: The comeback gave Daniels his first win as a starter since Oct. 5, 2025. Washington moved up from 27th to 25th in Fox Sports' rankings. Quinn's job security remains an open question.

stories.text: Home vs. Rams, Sunday 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Washington hosts Los Angeles at Northwest Stadium at 2-4-1. Watch how Daniels works without Burks and Brown. Both teams carry injuries in the secondary and on the line.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Simmons and Williams push Bears to 6-2

stories.text: Simmons makes a loud Bears debut in 34-17 rout of Seattle
stories.summary: The Bears sent two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder to Tennessee for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, then watched him get a sack in his first game. Seattle gained just 3.0 yards per play over the 48 snaps Simmons played. Chicago has won three straight and sits at 6-2.

stories.text: Bears list two non-participants ahead of Tampa Bay
stories.summary: Linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and running back Kyle Monangai (thumb and toe) did not practice Thursday. Lineman Theo Benedet (shoulder), defensive tackle Grady Jarrett (groin) and defensive back Malik Muhammad (toe) were limited. Tackle Braxton Jones is out for the season.

stories.text: Caleb Williams opens with a 17-play touchdown drive in Seattle
stories.summary: Williams completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 247 yards against the Seahawks. He went 10 of 15 for 109 yards and a touchdown on play-action. His opening march covered 80 yards in 17 plays, the longest opening drive for Chicago since 2007.

stories.text: 10: D'Andre Swift's rushing touchdowns lead the NFL
stories.summary: Swift ran 24 times for 57 yards and three touchdowns against Seattle. That pushed him to a league-high 10 rushing scores this season. The Bears also lead the league with 17 rushing touchdowns as a team.

stories.text: Bears host Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Chicago plays Tampa Bay (3-5) on Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC at Soldier Field. Watch how the Bears defense handles deep shots, since it has allowed 17 pass plays of 30 or more yards, the most in the league. The Bears rank second in sacks per pass attempt.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions fly to Miami without five starters

stories.text: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell shows progress after neck injury
stories.summary: Campbell left the 19-15 win over Minnesota on a backboard after a multi-player tackle in the second half. In a statement Wednesday he said he has full movement in his lower body and is improving in his upper body. Coach Dan Campbell said the team is encouraged by his progress.

stories.text: Lions rule out five, list three questionable for Miami
stories.summary: Center Cade Mays (ankle), edge DJ Wonnum (concussion), linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) and safety Kerby Joseph (knee) are out. Running back Sione Vaki (ankle), running back Jacob Saylors (neck) and receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) are questionable.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing per game
stories.summary: Gibbs has 773 rushing yards on 4.9 yards per carry and averages 110.4 yards per game, the best mark in the league. He has 8 rushing touchdowns and adds 34 catches for 285 yards and 2 more scores through the air.

stories.text: 15: Jared Goff touchdown passes against one interception
stories.summary: Goff has thrown 15 touchdowns with a single interception through seven games. He is completing 67.7 percent of his throws for 1,964 yards. Detroit owns the league's top-ranked offense.

stories.text: Lions visit Dolphins on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Detroit (5-2) plays at Miami (1-6) on Fox. The Lions defense gives up 2.6 passing touchdowns per game, the most in the league, and Malik Willis has multiple scoring passes in consecutive games for Miami.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers run game ranks last ahead of Patriots

stories.text: Packers carry a broken run game into Foxborough
stories.summary: Green Bay ranks 32nd in EPA per rush and has used 11 different offensive linemen this season. The 5-3 Packers hold the seventh seed in the NFC. They have lost at Detroit 20-17 and at Minnesota 39-22 this year and now face New England on Sunday.

stories.text: Packers rule out Micah Parsons and four others vs. Patriots
stories.summary: Parsons (knee), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), lineman Travis Glover (knee), lineman Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) are out. Cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and running backs MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and Chris Brooks (ankle) are questionable.

stories.text: Jordan Love keeps protecting the ball and the pocket
stories.summary: Love is 192 of 312 (61.5 percent) for 2,246 yards, 16 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. His sack rate of 4.3 percent is sixth best in the league. Christian Watson leads his targets with 42 catches for 708 yards and 6 touchdowns.

stories.text: 11 of 16: Trey Smack's field goal tally is the league's worst rate
stories.summary: Green Bay's kicker has made 11 of 16 field goal tries this season. That is the lowest success rate among the league's regular kickers.

stories.text: Packers visit Patriots on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at Gillette Stadium on Fox against New England (5-3). Quarterback Drake Maye has thrown or run for at least three touchdowns in five straight games, and wide receiver A.J. Brown is out for New England.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Wentz starts for Vikings vs. Bills on Monday

stories.text: Carson Wentz replaces injured Kyler Murray for Monday night
stories.summary: Murray strained his hamstring on a read-option run in the fourth quarter of the 19-15 loss to Detroit. Coach Kevin O'Connell called it more than a week-to-week injury but not an injured reserve case. Wentz starts at Buffalo, with Max Brosmer as his backup.

stories.text: Murray and Theo Jackson miss practice, Murray out Monday
stories.summary: Murray (hamstring) is out Monday, and safety Theo Jackson (quad) did not practice Thursday or Friday. Receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) and running back Demond Claiborne (knee) went from limited to no practice Friday. Tackle Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) was a full participant.

stories.text: Wentz has gone 4-3 as a Viking starter
stories.summary: Since signing in August 2025, Wentz has started six games and played most of a seventh. He has completed 63.9 percent of his throws for 1,492 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. Justin Jefferson has 44 catches for 615 yards and two scores in those games.

stories.text: 12: Vikings touchdowns tie the fewest ever for a 6-1 start
stories.summary: Minnesota has scored 12 touchdowns, second fewest in the NFL after the Chargers (9). That ties the fewest by any team that started 6-1 or better through seven games in the last 90 years.

stories.text: Vikings visit Bills on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Minnesota (6-1) meets Buffalo (6-1) at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Vikings defense allows the fewest points in the league at 13.3 per game, while their offense ranks 29th in rushing EPA against a Bills run defense ranked 25th.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons chase a reset in Madrid

stories.text: Falcons try to rebound in Madrid after a 16-0 loss
stories.summary: Atlanta landed in Spain on Wednesday and practiced at Real Madrid's training complex before Sunday's game against Cincinnati. The Falcons are coming off a shutout loss at Tampa Bay in heavy rain. Coach Kevin Stefanski says the trip can build team bonding, and receiver Jahan Dotson sees a chance to reset a season that has slipped to 3-5.

stories.text: Branch and Ebukam hurt, Pearce Jr. returns
stories.summary: Receiver Zachariah Branch and defensive end Samson Ebukam both injured hamstrings against Tampa Bay, and the AJC reports both are out for Madrid. Stefanski would not rule out either missing the Chiefs game after that. Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. returns from an eight-game suspension, and his role may grow with Ebukam sidelined. Divine Deablo (forearm), Brian Robinson Jr. and Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstrings) also missed the Tampa game.

stories.text: Jahan Dotson: 95 yards on two catches in the loss
stories.summary: Dotson caught two passes for 95 yards in Atlanta's 16-0 loss at Tampa Bay, one of the few bright spots on the day. He also takes over punt return duties with Branch hurt. The AJC says Dotson views the Madrid trip as a chance to reset the season.

stories.text: 32nd: Penix's rank among 35 QBs in completion over expected
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. ranks 32nd of 35 starting quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected, according to Sports Illustrated's Week 9 preview. He went 8 of 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions against Tampa Bay. Cincinnati's Joe Burrow leads the league in passing yards per game at 302.1.

stories.text: Falcons vs. Bengals in Madrid, Sunday 9:30 AM ET
stories.summary: Atlanta (3-5) faces Cincinnati (5-2) at Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday at 9:30 AM ET on NFL Network. Watch how the Falcons' secondary handles Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who both topped 100 yards in the Bengals' 43-36 overtime win over Tennessee. The Falcons also need their run game and run defense to recover after Tampa Bay ran for 324 yards.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers fire DC Evero, Wash steps in

stories.text: Panthers fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero
stories.summary: Carolina fired Evero on Oct. 30 after a 27-19 loss at Green Bay. Coach Dave Canales pointed to a collection of information over time and the need to build the defense's infrastructure. Defensive line coach Todd Wash is now interim coordinator and will call the plays. The defense ranked 22nd overall and last against the run.

stories.text: Four Panthers questionable, Moton out for the year
stories.summary: Corey Bullock, Will Lee III, Damien Lewis and Jaelan Phillips are listed as questionable for Denver. Tackle Taylor Moton, cornerback Jaycee Horn and Jonathon Brooks are on injured reserve, and Ikem Ekwonu is on the PUP list. Bullock left the Green Bay game with a quad injury, and Monroe Freeling started in Moton's place at right tackle.

stories.text: Bryce Young absorbs six sacks behind a hurt line
stories.summary: Young went down six times at Green Bay and faced pressure on 48.9 percent of his dropbacks, per Next Gen Stats. Under pressure he completed 6 of 16 passes for 46 yards and an interception. He wore a brace on his left knee, called it fine, and said injuries are no excuse. He has taken 64 pressures through seven games, second in the league.

stories.text: 12: games of 200-plus rushing yards allowed since 2024
stories.summary: Evero's defenses allowed 12 games of 200 or more rushing yards since 2024, the most in the league. Chicago ran for 291 yards and six touchdowns in Week 1, and Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards against Carolina in Week 7. Wash gets his first game plan against Denver on Sunday.

stories.text: Panthers host Broncos, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Carolina (3-4, first in the NFC South) hosts Denver (6-2) at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS. The Panthers have lost two straight and are 0-4 on the road. Watch the run defense under Wash against a Denver offense that leans on its defense to win games.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints return from bye with Tyson in play

stories.text: Rookie WR Jordyn Tyson returns to practice after the bye
stories.summary: Tyson, the No. 8 pick in the 2026 draft, practiced Wednesday for the first time since a preseason hamstring injury. The Saints are 2-5 and last in the NFC South, one and a half games behind first-place Carolina. His return gives a middling passing offense a possible lift as the team comes off its bye.

stories.text: Tyson, Banks questionable; Donaldson out vs. Browns
stories.summary: Running back CJ Donaldson is out with a shoulder and concussion issue. Receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring), tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle), tackle Asim Richards (thumb) and cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (shin) are questionable. Banks and Tyson both practiced in a limited role. Safety Justin Reid is expected to play after concussion-like symptoms.

stories.text: Tyler Shough threw 30 of 38 in the Paris loss
stories.summary: Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards with one touchdown and one interception in a 16-10 loss to the Steelers. He also led the Saints in rushing with seven yards on three carries. A hand injury earlier this season did not keep him out of practice.

stories.text: 69: pressures on Tyler Shough, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Shough has faced 69 pressures through seven games, the most of any quarterback in the league. Carolina's Bryce Young is second with 64. The number puts New Orleans' offensive line, with Banks and Richards both questionable, under a spotlight against Cleveland.

stories.text: Saints host Browns, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: New Orleans (2-5) hosts Cleveland (5-3) at the Caesars Superdome on Sunday, noon CT, on CBS. This is the first game after the bye. Watch whether Tyson plays and how the line holds up against pressure.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs win 16-0 without a completion

stories.text: Bucs beat Falcons 16-0 without completing a pass
stories.summary: Tampa Bay shut out Atlanta on a wet Sunday and ran for about 324 yards, a team single-game record. Baker Mayfield went 0 for 3 in his second game back from a thumb fracture. The defense produced four interceptions off Michael Penix Jr. The win is Tampa Bay's second in a row.

stories.text: Diaby out, Egbuka questionable for Chicago
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby is out with a knee injury after missing all three practices. Receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) is questionable after full practices Thursday and Friday. Tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) was limited Friday and carries no game designation. Mayfield practiced fully with his right thumb.

stories.text: Bucky Irving rushes for a career-high 170 yards
stories.summary: Irving carried 27 times for 170 yards and a 4-yard touchdown against Atlanta, a career high. He leads the team with 728 rushing yards and six touchdowns this season. Kenny Gainwell added 140 yards, including a 6-yard run that set the franchise single-game rushing record.

stories.text: 0: pass completions in a win, a first since 1974
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is the first team to win without a completion since Buffalo on Sept. 29, 1974, according to the Chicago Sun-Times. The Bucs ran for 324 yards, a single-game team record. Kicker Chase McLaughlin made all three of his field goals to move to 19 for 19 this season.

stories.text: Bucs at Bears, Sunday 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Tampa Bay (3-5) visits Chicago (6-2) at Soldier Field on Sunday Night Football, with Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth on the call. The Bucs lead the league in rushing offense and face Chicago's fourth-ranked run defense. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams carries a 104.6 passer rating, and Chicago added defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Minshew takes over as Cardinals starter

stories.text: Minshew replaces Brissett as Arizona's starting quarterback
stories.summary: Coach Mike LaFleur named Gardner Minshew the starter for Sunday at Seattle after he rallied the Cardinals from a 17-3 deficit in Dallas. Minshew went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns after Jacoby Brissett came out in the second half. Carson Beck moves up to the No. 2 job and Brissett drops to the emergency role.

stories.text: Three Cardinals ruled out, three more questionable vs. Seattle
stories.summary: Guard Jon Gaines (ankle), running back Bam Knight (concussion) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee) are out on Friday's report. Guard Isaiah Adams (ankle), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and defensive lineman Walter Nolen (ankle) are questionable. The offensive line takes the biggest hit with two starters sidelined.

stories.text: Allgeier posts a career day when Arizona's backfield runs thin
stories.summary: Tyler Allgeier ran 11 times for 147 yards, a career high, and scored on a 63-yard run, his longest ever. He added five catches for 44 yards and a touchdown. Allgeier was the only healthy back left once Bam Knight went into concussion protocol and Jeremiyah Love left with an ankle injury.

stories.text: 5-0: Cardinals keep winning at AT&T Stadium
stories.summary: Arizona beat Dallas 33-30 in overtime and is now 5-0 at AT&T Stadium. The Cardinals have won five straight against the Cowboys overall. Chad Ryland kicked the 42-yard winner after he missed an extra point with six seconds left in regulation.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Seahawks Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Arizona plays at Lumen Field on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 PM ET on FOX. Seattle will start Drew Lock because Sam Darnold is out. Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns when the Seahawks beat Arizona 31-7 in Week 2.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Garrett set to debut for Rams after knee surgery

stories.text: Myles Garrett expected to make Rams debut at Washington
stories.summary: Garrett played Week 1 in Australia, then had knee surgery and went on injured reserve. His 21-day practice window opened this week, and Sean McVay expects him to play Sunday barring setbacks. Garrett said he is happy to be back and wants to make the most of the time he has left this season.

stories.text: McDuffie, Parkinson and Curl questionable; Ferguson out
stories.summary: Tight end Terrance Ferguson is out after a hamstring injury in Friday's practice. Cornerback Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice all week and is questionable, along with tight end Colby Parkinson, safety Kam Curl, linebacker Grant Stuard and receiver Jordan Whittington. Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is out and headed to injured reserve.

stories.text: Corum finds room in the run game against the Chargers
stories.summary: Blake Corum averaged 5.8 yards after contact per carry against the Chargers, his best mark this season. Nine of his 11 carries were man-blocking runs, which gained 65 yards and produced his only touchdown. He also picked up 23 yards after forcing missed tackles.

stories.text: 369: Puka Nacua's receptions through 50 career games
stories.summary: Nacua's 369 catches are 23 more than any other player has through 50 games in NFL history. His 4,756 receiving yards in that span rank second, behind Justin Jefferson's 4,825.

stories.text: Rams at Commanders Sunday at 1 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland, on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. The Rams are 4-4 and have won two straight. Watch whether Garrett plays and how the secondary holds up if McDuffie sits.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Bosa and McCaffrey cleared after the bye

stories.text: Bosa and McCaffrey cleared to face the Raiders
stories.summary: Nick Bosa returns after missing five games with a calf injury. He went from limited work Wednesday and Thursday to a full practice Friday, and Kyle Shanahan said he is cleared to go. Christian McCaffrey, who strained a hamstring in Week 7, also practiced fully Friday with no game designation.

stories.text: Evans, Samuel and Kirk out, leaving San Francisco thin at receiver
stories.summary: Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) are all out, which takes three of the six receivers on the 53-man roster. Demarcus Robinson is questionable and likely to be activated from injured reserve after five missed games. KhaDarel Hodge could be elevated from the practice squad.

stories.text: Purdy aims to clean up after a two-interception loss
stories.summary: Brock Purdy went 27 of 40 for 288 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Week 7 loss at Atlanta. The second pick, thrown on third-and-9 with under three minutes left, ended a possible go-ahead drive. San Francisco had turned the ball over only six times in its first six games.

stories.text: 4-0: Atlanta's turnover edge in the 49ers' only loss
stories.summary: The Falcons took the ball away four times and gave it away none in their 29-20 win. Atlanta scored 13 points off those turnovers. Shanahan said four giveaways with zero takeaways makes it very hard to win.

stories.text: Raiders visit Levi's Stadium Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The 49ers host Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 PM ET on FOX after a Week 8 bye. The Raiders are 4-4 and coming off a 38-33 win over the Jets. Watch the 49ers' receiver depth and the return of Bosa.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Lock starts as Darnold sits with quad injury

stories.text: Darnold out against Arizona, Lock to start
stories.summary: Sam Darnold will miss Sunday's game with a quadriceps injury that Mike Macdonald called week to week. He hurt it on Seattle's last drive of the 34-17 Monday night loss to Chicago, after playing through a rib injury. Drew Lock starts and Jalen Milroe is the backup.

stories.text: Seven Seahawks out, including Cross, Nelson and Williams
stories.summary: Seattle ruled out quarterback Sam Darnold, tackle Charles Cross (ankle), guard Quenton Nelson (knee), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee), defensive tackles Leonard Williams (stinger) and Brandon Pili (back), and linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle). Linebacker Connor O'Toole (foot) is questionable. The offensive line loses two starters.

stories.text: Drew Lock steps in with a clean touchdown record
stories.summary: Lock has four touchdowns and no interceptions this season. In Week 2 he beat Arizona 31-7, completing 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns. He has spent the last two games as the emergency third quarterback because of forearm and elbow injuries.

stories.text: 985: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's receiving yards through eight games
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba had six catches for 118 yards and a touchdown against Chicago. His 985 yards lead the NFL by 259 and trail only Tyreek Hill's 1,014 in 2023 for the most through eight games in the Super Bowl era. It was his seventh game this season with 100 or more receiving yards.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Lumen Field Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Arizona on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 PM ET on FOX. The Seahawks are 4-4 and need a bounce back after Monday's 34-17 loss. Watch how Lock and a thinned offensive line handle Arizona's pass rush.
